name: Barbell Wrist Curl
cardText:
Barbell Wrist Curl
Novice
1
Grab a straight bar with a supinated (underhand) grip.
2
Kneel down next to a flat bench and place your forearms on the bench with your wrists just off the bench.
3
Let the barbell pull down on your wrists until they are extended.
4
Curl the barbell until your wrists are fully flexed.
5
Lower in a controlled manner and repeat.

name: Barbell Bent Over Row
cardText:
Barbell Bent Over Row
Intermediate
1
Grab a barbell with a shoulder width pronated or supinated grip.
2
Bend forward at your hips while maintaining a flat back.
3
Pull the weight toward your upper abdomen.
4
Lower the weight in a controlled manner and repeat.

name: Barbell Behind The Back Wrist Curl
cardText:
Barbell Behind The Back Wrist Curl
Intermediate
1
Stand straight and hold the barbell behind you using a pronated grip with your hands and feet shoulder-width apart.
2
Slowly curl your wrists in a semi-circular motion upwards.
3
Hold the barbell at the apex of the motion and then slowly lower the barbell back down to starting position.

name: Barbell Reverse Curl
cardText:
Barbell Reverse Curl
Advanced
1
Take a double overhand grip that's about shoulder width. Flex your elbows while keeping your elbows tucked in. Try not to let them flare out.
2
Curl until your forearm presses into your bicep. Then fully extend your elbows at the bottom of each rep.

name: Barbell Landmine Row
cardText:
Barbell Landmine Row
Intermediate
1
Position a barbell in a landmine or corner of a room and stand facing it with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2
Grasp the end of the barbell with a neutral grip, keeping your arms straight and your shoulders relaxed.
3
Bend at the hips and knees to lower your torso until it is almost parallel to the ground.
4
Pull the barbell towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together as you row the weight up.

name: Barbell Long Landmine Row
cardText:
Barbell Long Landmine Row
Advanced
1
Position a barbell in a landmine or corner of a room and stand facing it with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2
Grasp the end of the barbell with an overhand grip, keeping your arms straight and your shoulders relaxed.
3
Bend at the hips and knees to lower your torso until it is almost parallel to the ground.
4
Pull the barbell towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together as you row the weight up.

name: Barbell Meadows Row
cardText:
Barbell Meadows Row
Intermediate
1
Position a barbell in a landmine or corner of a room and stand facing sideways with a staggered stance and your feet shoulder-width apart.
2
Grasp the end of the barbell with an overhand grip, keeping your arms straight and your shoulders relaxed.
3
Bend at the hips and knees to lower your torso until it is almost parallel to the ground.
4
Pull the barbell towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together as you row the weight up.
5
*Named after the late John Meadows

name: Barbell Pronated Row
cardText:
Barbell Pronated Row
Intermediate
1
Grab the barbell with an overhand grip. Hinge forward while keeping your back flat until your torso is about parallel with the ground.
2
Let your arms hang freely.
3
Pull the bar to your torso while tucking your elbows in slightly.
4
Extend your elbows fully before initiating the next rep.

name: EZ Bar Reverse Preacher Curl
cardText:
EZ Bar Reverse Preacher Curl
Novice
1
Sit on preacher bench, grip EZ bar overhand at shoulder width, elbows resting on pad.
2
Curl bar towards chin, keep elbows stable.
3
Lower bar slowly to starting position, maintaining control throughout.

name: Ez Bar Reverse Curl
cardText:
Ez Bar Reverse Curl
Beginner
1
Take a double overhand grip that's about shoulder width. Flex your elbows while keeping your elbows tucked in. Try not to let them flare out.
2
Curl until your forearm presses into your bicep. Then fully extend your elbows at the bottom of each rep.

name: Ez Bar Reverse Spider Curl
cardText:
Ez Bar Reverse Spider Curl
Beginner
1
Lay on an incline bench and hold the EZ bar with your elbows extended.
2
From this starting position, curl the bar up towards your shoulders, keeping your elbows close to your body and your core engaged.
3
Slowly lower the bar back down to the starting position, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
